name: Nextpower

logo.source: investors.nextpower.com header logo (NXP_Logo_Horizontal_White.svg on s21.q4cdn.com); no Wikipedia or Commons logo exists. The site publishes only a white version, so it is saved here with the fill set to black

description: Nextpower (renamed from Nextracker) sells the steel structures, motors, controls and software that tilt solar panels to follow the sun at utility-scale solar plants, and says it has been the global leader in solar trackers by gigawatts shipped for ten straight years (over 160 GW shipped by March 31, 2026). Customers are the engineering-and-construction firms and developers that build solar farms; 77% of fiscal 2026 revenue shipped to the US. It has been adding the rest of the plant (foundations, steel frames, electrical balance-of-system parts, robotic inspection, soiling monitors) by acquisition. Profit leans on a US manufacturing tax credit (Section 45X) earned by its American suppliers and, since 2025 in some cases, by Nextpower directly: $379.9 million of 45X vendor credits reduced fiscal 2026 costs, against $697.3 million of operating income.

gics.note: Wikipedia 'List of S&P 400 companies', raw wikitext read 2026-10-27: Nextpower (NXT, Nasdaq), Industrials, Electrical Components & Equipment, Fremont, California. The list gives only sector and sub-industry, so industry group and industry are left null.

hq.note: Cover page of the FY2026 10-K: 6200 Paseo Padre Parkway, Fremont, CA 94555

employees.note: About 1,993 full-time employees, over 578 in technical or engineering roles and over 500 in R&D; eight offices, including a Hyderabad, India office with over 542 employees (FY2026 10-K)

businessLines.name: Solar trackers and plant technology (single segment)
businessLines.how: Sells tracker hardware, controls and software project by project to solar EPC firms, developers and owners, increasingly under multi-year volume commitment agreements with deposits, and adds foundations, frames and electrical parts to each plant. The 45X credits earned on US-made torque tubes and fasteners lower its cost of goods.
businessLines.description: Solar tracking systems (flagship NX Horizon, independent-row, self-powered, with terrain-following XTR variants) with TrueCapture yield-management software; plus foundations, steel frames, electrical balance of systems (eBOS, from the 2025 Bentek purchase), robotic inspection and fire detection (OnSight), soiling monitoring (Fracsun) and power conversion technology.

operatingProfit.note: FY2025 $639.1M; FY2024 $587.1M. Includes $379.9M of 45X vendor credits shown as a reduction of cost (FY2025 $224.9M)

brands.name: NX Horizon (flagship tracker)
brands.share: Not separately reported; the most-deployed tracker in the portfolio

brands.name: Origami Solar (steel panel frames; acquired September 8, 2025)
Ojjo and Spinex Systems (foundations; acquired June and July 2024)
Saudi Arabia joint venture with Abdullah Abunayyan Investment Holding

whatsNext.text: Acquisition of Zimmermann PV-Steel Group (Germany) for up to EUR 330 million: about EUR 180 million cash at closing, EUR 105 million in Nextpower Class A shares, and up to EUR 45 million contingent cash; agreement signed June 21, 2026; closing date not stated in the 8-K
